title: Incremental VPC Upgrade & Hybrid On‑Prem Onboarding — Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for onboarding customer VPCs that require hybrid setups (customer on‑prem ↔ Redwood private VPC) and for running incremental Terraform-driven upgrades of existing private-deployments. It captures a pragmatic, low-risk migration path, module versioning guidance, and operator checklists for SEs and SREs.

Scope:
- Applies to customer VPCs connected via transit/peering (AWS/Azure/GCP) or dedicated VPN/MPLS circuits.
- Covers upgrades of networking TF modules, route/failover changes, and IP re-mapping scenarios.
- Does NOT cover Kubernetes app-level migrations, certificate rotations, or tenant DB migrations (handled in separate runbooks).

Audience:
- Solutions Engineers onboarding customers for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments
- Platform & SRE teams performing upgrades and maintenance windows
- Developer-owners of Terraform modules in infra repo

Background / Motivation:
We repeatedly see two failure modes during customer VPC upgrades: (1) large-surface upgrades attempted in a single wave causing dependent routes/services to break, and (2) insufficient testing of IPv6 and dual-stack behaviour. This playbook recommends incremental, reversible steps, explicit terraform module compatibility rules, and a lightweight validation matrix.

Upgrade Principles (TL;DR):
- Small changes, canary first: prefer one-customer / one-subnet canaries.
- Versioned modules with clear compatibility matrix (major = breaking).
- Keep control-plane changes atomic but separate from data-plane cutovers.
- Explicit rollback plan for every change and automated smoke tests.

TF Module Versioning & Migration Strategy:
- Semver for TF modules: major = breaking network topology changes (e.g., replace TGW w/ peering), minor = new optional outputs/inputs, patch = bugfixes.
- Migration pattern: introduce new module (vN+1) alongside old one (vN) and add compatibility shims in code: i.e., we create a transitional layer that maps old outputs to new expected inputs. Avoid in-place destructive replacements.
- Provider pinning: every customer workspace must pin provider and module versions in their locked state file. During upgrades we supply a best-practice update script (see linked repo).
- Module change checklist (for module owners): document new inputs, mark required vs optional, provide one-line migration note, include terraform plan examples that show null-diff for compatibility cases.

Phased Onboarding / Upgrade Steps (high level):
1) Discovery (S: -14 to -7 days)
   - Gather: CIDR blocks (v4/v6), route tables, NACLs, existing TGW/transit info, peering IDs, BGP ASNs, customer maintenance windows, contact list.
   - Confirm: which services require pinned IPs, egress constraints, SOC/PCI controls.
   - Output: "onboarding-factsheet" (one-pager) and precheck script run.

2) Design & Preflight (S: -7 to -3 days)
   - Sketch topology: show transit/peering, NAT placement, egress firewall, and any local eBGP.
   - Decide: Cutover mode (hot-swap vs phased), IPv6 enablement, whether to use TGW or direct peering.
   - Run synthetic tests using staging VPC mirrored to customer settings.

3) Staging & Terraform Dry Runs (S: -3 to -1 days)
   - Create isolated staging workspace pinning existing module versions.
   - Run 'terraform plan' for vN→vN+1 across staging, capture diffs.
   - Smoke test connectivity scripts (BGP session up, route visibility, iperf/lightweight tcp checks).

4) Canary (Day 0)
   - Choose a low-risk subnet or single AZ to apply changes.
   - Apply module upgrade in canary workspace.
   - Run automated validation (see Test Matrix).
   - Hold for observation window (min 60 minutes for BGP convergence checks).

5) Gradual Rollout (Day 0+1..N)
   - Expand to remaining subnets/regions in waves (document wave sizes e.g., 25% of AZs at a time).
   - Monitor costs/latency and application errors.

6) Cutover & Clean-up (final wave)
   - Remove compatibility shims, deprecate old modules after 7 days of stable telemetry.
   - Update customer-facing runbook and compliance evidence.

Networking specifics & gotchas:
- BGP timers: ensure customer and Redwood sides agree on hold/timers; mismatched timers cause flaps.
- Asymmetric routing: validate return path via flow logs; add temporary stateful NAT rules if needed.
- MTU: on-prem links often have smaller MTU; test with iperf -M and adjust PMTU/fragmentation.
- IPv6: Many customers have partial IPv6 rollout; do not enable dual-stack in mass without a canary. Provide explicit fallback to IPv4-only for services that don’t support IPv6.
- TGW vs Peering: TGW simplifies scale but can block transitive routes for some partner topologies — validate with route table diagrams.

Testing Matrix (automated + manual):
- Connectivity smoke: BGP up, route table contains expected prefixes, security groups allow expected ports (automated).
- Latency/Throughput: 95/99p token latency checks for inference path (automated with short spike tests).
- Functional: API handshake with private endpoint, token validation and sample inference (automated).
- Security/compliance: Verify flow logs, VPC flow export, KMS access patterns (manual review + checklist).
- Edge cases: IPv6-only host reachability, fragmented packets, MTU drop (manual tests).

Observability expectations during upgrades:
- Minimum dashboards to watch: route churn, BGP flaps, private endpoint 5xx rates, per-token latency SLO breaches, cost anomalies.
- Alerts: route-change alert (severity P2), endpoint-5xx (P1), BGP-down (P1).
- Logging: collect both sides’ flow logs and syslogs for the duration + 48h post rollout.

Rollback plan (must be executable within 30 minutes):
- Trigger conditions: persistent 5xx > 3% across 10 mins, BGP instability > 3 reconnections in 5 mins, or security policy breach.
- Steps:
   1. Run automated rollback script to re-apply previous TF module version workspace (stored state snapshot).
   2. Re-establish previous route tables and remove new NAT/egress rules.
   3. Notify customer and open incident with SRE-runbook link.
- Post-rollback: run postmortem, mark module minor with fix plan, coordinate follow-up re-deploy window.

Communication & Scheduling:
- Use the standard "PD-Outage-Notice" template for maintenance windows.
- SE to own customer comms for the canary and final cutover; SRE owns monitoring and rollback.
- Record decisions in the onboarding-factsheet and link to Jira ticket.

Action Items / Open Questions (triage board):
- [ ] Build a one-click staging workspace initializer script (owner: eng-platform).
- [ ] Add IPv6 compatibility gates to module CI (owner: applied-ml infra).
- [ ] Define golden test vectors for inference smoke tests behind private endpoints (owner: solutions-eng).
- [?] Should we standardize on TGW for all new customers or keep case-by-case? (open; escalate to architecture).

Appendix A — Example terraform migration pattern (pseudo):
- keep_old_module = module.vpc_old
- deploy_new_module = module.vpc_new
- compatibility_bridge: local.new_to_old = { subnet_id = module.vpc_new.subnet_id != null ? module.vpc_new.subnet_id : module.vpc_old.subnet_id }
- apply in canary workspace, validate, then promote to global workspace.

Appendix B — Useful links and tickets:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/VPC+Reference+Patterns
- TF modules repo (internal): github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules
- Jira epic: PD-1987 (Hybrid VPC migration epic)

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep playbook minimal — field teams need copy-paste checklists.
- Capture one end-to-end recorded session for new SEs (video).
- Revisit this doc after 3rd real customer run to fold in lessons.
